name: Superfiliate
summary: Creator-led growth for D2C brands: run influencer, affiliate and referral programs in one platform across Shopify, Meta and TikTok Shop, with discovery, automation, gifting and revenue tracking.
best_for: e-commerce brands turning customers and creators into affiliates with branded co-branded storefronts, if the volume justifies a demo-quoted platform fee
skip_if: you're testing affiliate marketing for the first time: there is no self-serve entry and no published price, so the first step is a sales call about a program that is not yet producing
honest_knock: The price is no longer hidden, and it is high. The Shopify listing prints four tiers from $1,500 a month to $5,000 a month, each plus 3% of the revenue your affiliates generate, with a 21 day trial. The cards do not say what separates the tiers, and the vendor's own pricing page describes a custom subscription built on the channels you activate and your trailing twelve months of ecommerce revenue without printing an amount, so ask for the tier definitions and the way the 3% is counted in writing. On fit rather than price: this is built for brands already running creator and affiliate programs, and it is overkill if you are testing your first affiliate offer.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/superfiliate and superfiliate.com/pricing; earlier reads 25 August, 5 and 24 September 2026, when the listing published a single plan called Custom and no amount) The Shopify App Store listing now prints four tiers, billed in USD every 30 days, each with a 21 day free trial and each adding 3% of the revenue generated by your affiliates: Tier 1 $1,500 a month, Tier 2 $2,499, Tier 3 $3,499 and All access $5,000. The listing's header reads From $1,500/month with a free trial available, and the cards give no definition of what separates the tiers, so we cannot say what each one includes. The wording of September, a single plan named Custom that was free to install and needed an active Superfiliate subscription, is gone from the cards. superfiliate.com/pricing, which returned 404 on 5 and 24 September 2026, now loads. It says Superfiliate is priced as a custom monthly subscription built on the channels you want to activate and your trailing twelve months of ecommerce revenue, with no charge per creator, per click or per program, and it prints no amount. The range of roughly $299 to $999 a month that an earlier version of this dossier carried traced to no dated source and is wrong against the listing: the lowest published tier is $1,500 a month. The listing shows 5.0 from 44 reviews.

schema_offer.description: Tier 1, per month plus 3% of the revenue generated by your affiliates, with a 21 day free trial; Tier 2 $2,499, Tier 3 $3,499 and All access $5,000 on the same terms; printed on the Shopify listing, while superfiliate.com/pricing describes a custom subscription and prints no amount. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-17.

price_history.method: Stable = every amount on the vendor's pricing page identical across >= 3 of our reads over >= 30 days. A change is listed only after we confirmed the new price on the page, with a verbatim quote. Differences in raw readings are never published on their own.

Commission never changes what a record says, and products are not ranked by commission. Where it is false the link is the vendor's plain site.

open_questions.question: Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?
